title: 01. Hello Python
lesson: In Python, the print() function is used to display text on the screen. Anything inside the quotation marks inside the parentheses is what gets printed.
desc: Write a print() command that outputs the exact text: Hello, World!

title: 02. Multiple Lines
lesson: You can place multiple print() statements one after another. Each statement will automatically output its result on a new line.
desc: Print Python on the first line, and is awesome on the second line using two separate print statements.

title: 03. Code Comments
lesson: Lines in your code that start with the # symbol are comments. Python completely ignores them when running the code. They are used to leave notes for humans.
desc: Add a comment that says # Learning Python, then print Ready on the next line.
starterCode: # Add your comment and print statement below

title: 04. Syntax Errors
lesson: Python is strict about grammar—this is called syntax. If you forget a closing quotation mark or parenthesis, Python will throw a SyntaxError.
desc: Fix the broken code in the editor so it successfully prints Hello Again.

title: 05. Math Inside Print
lesson: You don't always need quotes. If you pass numbers into print() with math operators (like + or *), Python calculates the answer before printing it.
desc: Print the result of 10 + 15 without using quotation marks.

title: 06. Multi-line Strings
lesson: If you want a single string to span across multiple lines naturally without writing multiple print statements, you can use triple quotes: """.
desc: Use triple quotes inside a print() statement to output: Line One Line Two
starterCode: # Print multi-line string using triple quotes

title: 07. Escape Characters
lesson: You can insert a newline directly inside a single-string print statement by using the escape character \n.
desc: Print Alpha and Beta on separate lines using a single print() statement and \n.

title: 08. Tab Spacing
lesson: Another useful escape character is \t, which inserts a horizontal tab (indentation) into your printed text.
desc: Print the word Indent: followed by a tab character \t and the word Accepted.

title: 09. Printing Multiple Arguments
lesson: You can print multiple items in a single print statement by separating them with commas. Python automatically adds a space between them.
desc: Print the words Code and Level and 1 separated by commas.

title: 10. Level 1 Checkpoint
lesson: Time to test everything you've learned in Level 1 into a final standalone script.
desc: Write a script with a comment # Complete and a print statement that outputs LEVEL_ONE_COMPLETE.
